items.title: What the universe expands into
items.claim: When cosmologists say the universe is expanding, what is the most accurate description of where it expands to?

options.text: The metric of space itself increases distances between unbound objects; there is no external 'outside'

items.reveal_title: Expansion is of the metric, not into a container
items.reveal:
General relativity describes the metric of space evolving with time. The FLRW metric encodes this expansion.

Gravitationally bound systems (galaxies, the Local Group) are not expanding with the cosmic flow.
items.why: Cosmology requires letting go of everyday intuitions about space as a fixed stage.

items.title: How long photons take to escape the Sun
items.claim: A photon generated in the Sun's core takes how long, on average, to reach the surface?
items.reveal_title: Tens of thousands of years through a dense plasma
items.reveal:
The radiative zone is so opaque that photons random-walk outward. Mitalas and Sills (1992) modelled the escape time at about 10,000 to 170,000 years depending on assumptions.

Once free, the photon reaches Earth in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.
items.why: The dramatic part of a photon's journey is hidden inside its source, not its trip across space.

items.title: Lunar samples returned
items.claim: How much lunar material did the six Apollo missions return to Earth in total?
items.reveal:
Apollo 11 returned about 22 kg; later missions returned larger samples. Soviet Luna robotic missions returned around 0.3 kg.

China's Chang'e 5 (2020) returned around 1.7 kg.
items.why: Sample-return missions remain extremely costly per gram delivered, shaping research priorities.
